title: Design and Develop a Smart Mobile Medical-Waste Collection and Segregation System
description:
• Description Healthcare facilities generate large volumes of biomedical waste that require safe, compliant, and efficient handling. Manual collection and segregation increase the risk of contamination, operational inefficiencies, and regulatory challenges.
Design and develop an AI-powered, battery-electric autonomous mobile system that automates the collection, identification, segregation, and digital tracking of biomedical waste across hospitals. The solution should leverage AI-enabled vision systems to classify waste, intelligently segregate it into designated compartments, and provide end-to-end traceability while minimizing human exposure to hazardous materials and improving safety, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance.
Using Autodesk Fusion, students must demonstrate a complete product development lifecycle-from concept ideation to manufacturing-ready product, delivering an innovative, scalable, and solution for next-generation healthcare waste management.
• Participation Guidelines For Idea Submission:
• Each student team will submit a PowerPoint presentation (5-7 Slides) with conceptual sketches, research, and relevant images.
• NO design files are required at this stage. The actual design must be created ONLY during the Grand Finale.
• Designs should be created using ONLY Autodesk Fusion and not copied or taken from any other source.
• AI Generated content is NOT ALLOWED.
For Grand Finale:
Students must use Autodesk Fusion within the given time period and present:
• PPT explaining the final project
• Public link of the fully developed Autodesk Fusion design model
• Use of Generative Design for optimization will be an added advantage.
• Simulation and Analysis will be advantageous
• Motion study and exploded assembly view
• Hi-res rendered images
• Design should be capable of developing a prototype with a focus on Cost, Manufacturability, Scalability, and Quality.
Note: Teams coming with pre-designed files will be disqualified.
• Attach Marking Criteria Table here*
• Faculty (SIH SPOC) Form Teams choosing to submit idea for Autodesk’s problem statement are required to request their faculty (SIH SPOC) to fill this 'Mandatory Form'.
• Autodesk Fusion
• Autodesk Fusion is a cloud-based 3D modeling, CAD, CAM, CAE, and PCB software platform for professional product design and manufacturing.
• Students and educators can click here to get FREE access to Fusion.
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, generative, autonomous applied to a medtech / biotech / healthtech problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (5/5): reaches a broad public/citizen base within MedTech / BioTech / HealthTech. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on model, compliance. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (5/5): built to extend across states/users with modest rework. Total 25/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: Smart Mobile Medical-Waste Collection and Segregation System (Autodesk Fusion Design Challenge)

overview.in_plain_terms: Design (not build) an AI-vision-equipped autonomous robot that collects and sorts biomedical waste in hospitals, minimizing human contact with hazardous materials, as a concept idea submission with sketches and research rather than a working robot.
overview.why_it_matters: Manual biomedical waste handling is genuinely risky for hospital staff. A well-thought-out autonomous concept demonstrates real engineering thinking toward reducing that exposure and improving compliance.
pain_points: Manual biomedical waste collection and segregation increases contamination risk.
Operational inefficiencies and regulatory compliance challenges from manual handling.
No integrated autonomous system exists for end-to-end biomedical waste identification, segregation, and tracking.
overview.background: Healthcare facilities generate large volumes of biomedical waste requiring safe, compliant handling, and manual processes increase contamination risk and operational inefficiency.
overview.whats_being_asked: An idea/concept submission (PowerPoint with sketches and research, no design files required) for an AI-powered, battery-electric autonomous mobile system automating biomedical waste collection, classification, segregation, and digital tracking.
expected_solution: Autonomous mobile collection and segregation mechanism concept.
Conceptual product-development lifecycle documentation (idea submission stage, PPT only, no design files).

analysis.innovation_scope_note: This is explicitly an idea-submission-stage challenge (PPT only, no design files required for this round), a lighter-weight conceptual pitch rather than a working build or even a full CAD deliverable like the sibling Autodesk PS.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Effort goes into research, conceptual sketching, and clear presentation of a product concept, not working code or detailed CAD/CAM at this submission stage.

competitive_landscape.note: Combines a genuinely compelling healthcare-safety application with an accessible submission format (PPT/sketches), likely draws a broader range of participants than the CAD/CAM-only Autodesk PS.

innovation.note: Judged on genuine concept creativity, research depth, and real-world engineering intent, not code or working hardware.

invention.note: Judged on how well-researched and thoughtfully engineered the conceptual product-development narrative is.

technical_feasibility.tag: Very Comfortable for this Submission Stage
technical_feasibility.note: A PPT-based idea submission with sketches and research is genuinely achievable in 36 hours by most teams, this is the most accessible of the Autodesk-cluster PS.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuine, relatable impact story (reducing human exposure to hazardous medical waste) even at the concept stage.

architecture.note: Not applicable, this stage requires conceptual clarity, not working architecture.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, notably more accessible than its Autodesk-cluster siblings since it's explicitly an idea-submission stage (no design files required). Real research grounding (actual biomedical waste categories, real classification challenges) is what separates a strong concept from a generic pitch.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Explicitly an idea-submission stage with PPT and sketches, no CAD/CAM tool proficiency required unlike the sibling Autodesk PS, genuinely accessible to a broader range of teams.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: A generic, unresearched concept pitch without real grounding in actual biomedical waste categories, classification challenges, and regulatory requirements would read as superficial.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Research actual biomedical waste categorization standards (e.g. color-coded segregation categories used in real hospital waste management) to ground your concept in genuine domain accuracy, not an invented classification scheme.

idea_0_4: Research real biomedical waste categorization and segregation standards (actual color-coded category systems used in healthcare waste management).
Sketch your autonomous system concept: mobility, vision-based classification, segregation mechanism, tracking.
Split: one person on research/technical concept, one on sketches/visual presentation.
prototype_4_22: Develop detailed conceptual sketches of your autonomous system.
Research and document your AI-vision classification approach conceptually (what waste categories, what visual/sensor cues distinguish them).
integration_22_30: Compile your full concept narrative: problem, solution, technical approach, expected impact.
Research and cite real regulatory/compliance considerations your concept addresses.
Refine sketches for clarity and professional presentation.
polish_30_36: Finalize your 5-7 slide PowerPoint presentation per the submission requirements.
Rehearse presenting your concept's grounding in real biomedical waste management practice.
Prepare to discuss the path from this concept to a working prototype.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Ground your concept explicitly in real biomedical waste categorization standards and cite genuine regulatory compliance considerations, that research depth is what separates a credible engineering concept from a generic 'robot sorts trash' pitch.

strengths: Explicitly accessible idea-submission format, no CAD/CAM tool proficiency required.
Genuinely compelling, relatable healthcare-safety impact story.
weaknesses: Easy to produce a generic, unresearched concept without real domain grounding.
Concept-stage evaluation rewards research depth and clarity over technical build evidence.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Balanced, accessible to a general team without specialized CAD/CAM skill requirements.
team_fit.approach: Research real biomedical waste management standards early, this grounding differentiates a credible concept from a generic pitch.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Research synthesis and presentation drafting support.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Ensuring the concept is grounded in real biomedical waste categorization and regulatory practice, not generic or invented classification schemes.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-generated concept pitch without real domain research could misrepresent actual biomedical waste categories or regulatory requirements, undermining the concept's credibility.

data_resource_availability.status: Real biomedical waste categorization and management standards are publicly documented and should be researched and cited directly.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not applicable, real standards research is achievable and expected for this concept submission.

judge_qna.question: What real biomedical waste categorization standard does your concept's classification system reflect?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Cite the specific real categorization standard you researched (color-coded segregation categories used in actual healthcare waste management), don't present an invented classification scheme.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would your AI vision system actually distinguish between these real categories visually?

judge_qna.question: What's the realistic path from this concept to an actual working prototype?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Discuss the real engineering challenges ahead honestly, reliable waste-type classification, safe handling mechanisms, regulatory certification, this is a concept stage, be clear about what validation and development would follow.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's the single hardest technical challenge in actually building this?
